description:
## Question

How do `tk` and `nix` on a client reach the build service — endpoint discovery, credentials, `.buckconfig`/`[buck2_re_client]` and execution-platform settings, Nix substituters and trusted keys, and derivation submission?

## Context

Map turnkey-wit: clients are GitHub Actions runners (default), laptops, and a service-owned client host; clients submit work, never results; clients speak only REAPI and the Nix binary-cache protocol. The buck2 client is thin under remote execution: it needs the prelude and cells locally to evaluate BUCK files, but not compilers. This ticket redesigns turnkey-lbe's gaps G6 (`buck2.remoteCache` options, turnkey-lbe.7), G7 (test runner writing to a remote, turnkey-lbe.8 — contradicted by the trust rule), G8 (tiering the per-user bazel-remote, turnkey-lbe.9) and G9 (CI closure to Cachix, turnkey-lbe.10). Inputs: GitHub identity research, "Which results are shared…", "What does the executor need…", "What are the building blocks…". Current code: `nix/devenv/turnkey/buck2.nix` (generated `.buckconfig`, testCache options), `src/cmd/tk/`, `src/cmd/turnkey-test-runner/`.

## Decide (grilling)

1. turnkey module options (names, defaults, secret handling via `$VAR` in `http_headers`), and how `tk` obtains a short-lived credential per client kind.
2. What `tk` does when the service is unreachable (the ~45 s buck2 retry then mass failure, noted in ADR 0001 consequences) — probe and fall back to local?
3. How the client gets new cells built (submits derivations; waits) before buck2 runs; substituter and `trusted-public-keys` config.
4. Local tier: keep the per-user bazel-remote for client-computed results/test caching? Relationship to remote results.
5. The slim CI client closure (what a GitHub runner must realise) and what replaces pushing to Cachix.
6. Keep/rewrite/close decisions for turnkey-lbe.7, .8, .9, .10.

## Output

Resolution comment; `docs/specs/build-service.md` section "Client"; update the lbe children.
title: How do tk and nix on a client reach the build service?
